item.title: Massively multiplayer browser games on stateless pages and a relational database, a tutorial on their construction
item.description: arXiv:2611.33256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A massively multiplayer browser game is a persistent world that many players change through ordinary web pages, with no client to install. This work is a tutorial for a developer or developer who wants to structure such a game from the start, from the overall organisation into modules to the protocols between players. The running example is the open-source role-playing game Naruto! Nigeru, whose engine keeps the whole game state in a relational database and uses no third-party library. The tutorial presents the overall view of the game, how its code is separated into modules, which technologies it uses and which ones it avoids, and then each mechanism as a design decision with its alternatives, namely the request cycle, the data model, the identity of the player without sessions, the world map computed from a hash of the coordinates, the turn-based combat, the economy under simultaneous requests, the trade and duel protocols, the ways a page waits for another player, and the content and languages. It closes with a suggested order of construction and the lessons of the example. The example has 25,930 lines of code in 9 feature modules over a core of 2,364 lines.
item.dc:creator: \'E. O. Rodrigues

item.title: Representing and Animating Piano-Hinged Solids as Non-Manifold Cell Complexes: The Magic Photo Cube
item.description: arXiv:2611.33505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Piano-hinged solids are articulated structures consisting of rigid solid components connected along edges, allowing relative rotations while preserving their connectivity. We propose representing such structures as a class of edge-connected non-manifold cell complexes, in which the components and their hinge relationships are encoded through cell incidences rather than separate geometric hinge elements. This representation provides a unified framework for describing the geometry, connectivity, and admissible motions of articulated solids. We demonstrate the approach using the magic photo cube, an assembly of eight cubical cells connected by eight edge hinges. Each cell maintains a persistent identity and local coordinate frame, while successive folding operations transport hinge axes through rigid transformations. We reconstruct two distinct three-stage folding sequences and analyze their resulting configurations. Although the sequences produce compact cubes at different positions and orientations in a fixed reference frame, numerical analysis demonstrates that their terminal configurations are rigidly equivalent as labeled, oriented assemblies under a single proper rigid transformation. The example illustrates how an edge-connected non-manifold representation can support geometric modeling, animation, and configuration analysis while preserving the identities and incidence relationships of the constituent cells. An accompanying interactive web-based simulator, implemented in JavaScript and WebGL, is publicly available at https://people.tamu.edu/~ergun/software/magic_cube.
item.dc:creator: Ergun Akleman

item.title: M\"obiuString: Structured String Art via Optimizing Generatrices on the M\"obius Strip
item.description: arXiv:2611.33918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: String art is a worldwide handicraft that mimics an image with straight strings stretched between boundary pins. Existing image-driven methods primarily optimize individual strings for reconstruction fidelity, leaving the global organization of the strings weakly controlled.In this paper, we introduce the generatrix on the M\"obius strip of unordered boundary-point pairs to formalize families of strings with finite generatrices, enabling explicit control over their arrangement. Based on this new formalization, we propose M\"obiuString, a framework for generating structured, multi-color string art under a prescribed string budget. As an initialization, we place pins along boundaries of image-derived regions and select candidate string segments near each generatrix in the homeomorphic pin-index plane. During the iterative optimization, a 2DGS-based differentiable renderer jointly optimizes generatrix parameters and colors on multiple layers, while periodic discrete re-search revises string families to escape poor local configurations.To our knowledge, M\"obiuString is the first automatic image-based method to generate string art with a structured string organization with freeform region boundaries. Evaluations with two datasets and a user study demonstrate the outperformance of M\"obiuString over baselines.
item.dc:creator: Xinding Zhu, Hanni Bao, Xinye Yang, Qinyi Wang, Xu Yuzhong, Jiazhou Chen

item.title: Revisiting Monocular In-Hand Object Scanning: Dataset, Pose Estimation, and Surface Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.33824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-Hand Object Scanning (IHOS) from monocular video captured by a commodity smartphone holds immense potential to democratize 3D digitization for non-expert users, facilitating applications in digital archiving, augmented reality, and custom fabrication. Yet, IHOS remains largely understudied due to a lack of realistic datasets and systematic benchmarks. To bridge this gap, we introduce ToysRUs, a high-quality dataset featuring diverse figurines captured by 4K Ultra High-Definition (UHD) monocular videos. Studying IHOS from first principles, we examine structure-from-motion (SfM) for camera pose estimation, which is key to IHOS. We identify two key challenges: small baselines between consecutive frames, and sparse feature matches across large-view, long-range frames, further exacerbated by dynamic hand occlusions. Guided by these insights, we propose performing SfM on video sub-sequences sampled at sufficient angular intervals, and iteratively stitches the corresponding sub-trajectories into a unified global trajectory. Furthermore, for high-fidelity surface reconstruction, we introduce occlusion-aware 2D Gaussian Splatting, which incorporates opacity rendering and omits the opacity loss on hand regions. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms existing approaches, including neural implicit representations and 3D foundation models, in both geometric accuracy and photometric fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu, Jeeeun Kim, Shu Kong

item.title: SIA: Selective Image Analogy
item.description: arXiv:2611.33894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Image analogy transfers a demonstrated transformation from a before/after pair (A, A') to a new query image B. Existing methods assume all changes in (A, A') should be fully transferred, limiting flexibility when users want only a subset of the demonstrated edits. We introduce Selective Image Analogy (SIA), a new setting where a single demonstration pair encodes multiple edits, and the user selects at inference time which edits to apply to B. To support this, we curate a multi-edit analogy dataset with full-edit and partial-edit targets. We then train a model that first learns to transfer the complete demonstrated transformation, and then gains selective control through a mask-aligned suppression mechanism: a token-gated LoRA that restricts adapter updates to suppressed edit tokens during denoising, paired with a concept suppression vector that weakens the selected tokens in the text embeddings before denoising. Together, these components allow SIA to suppress unwanted edits that remain visible in A', while preserving the user-selected ones, all without requiring a new demonstration pair for each edit combination. We perform extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations along with user studies to demonstrate the efficacy of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Amirhossein Alimohammadi, Kian Izadpanah, Bardiya Kariminia, Yiorgos Chrysanthou, Ali Mahdavi-Amiri

item.title: 3DSS: 3D Surface Splatting for Inverse Rendering
item.description: arXiv:2605.05876v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present 3D Surface Splatting (3DSS), the first differentiable surface splatting renderer for physically-based inverse rendering from multi-view images. Our central insight is that surface separation, which groups the surfels covering a pixel by the surface they sample, can be formulated with the reconstruction kernels themselves: two surfels sample the same surface when their kernels overlap in depth. Compositing each resulting surface layer with a coverage opacity derived from its accumulated Elliptical Weighted Average (EWA) weight yields anti-aliased silhouettes and informative visibility gradients at sparsely covered edges. With forward microfacet shading under co-optimized HDR environment lighting, 3DSS jointly recovers shape, spatially-varying BRDF, and illumination, and its oriented surfels convert directly into meshes by oriented-point surface reconstruction. On the real-world Stanford-ORB and the TensoIR Synthetic benchmarks, 3DSS outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-based and major comparable implicit and Gaussian-based methods in novel view synthesis and relighting, with geometry on par with the strongest baselines.
item.dc:creator: Mae Younes, Adnane Boukhayma

item.title: Instant NuRec: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstruction for Driving Scene Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2607.14203v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: 3D simulation platforms are critical for autonomous driving because they enable end-to-end policy evaluation, thereby reducing development costs and improving safety. In recent years, neural simulation has become predominant, with methods such as NuRec playing a central role; however, these methods remain relatively slow and typically require per-scene tuning. In this work, we present Instant NuRec, a feed-forward neural reconstruction model that turns a short multi-view driving log into a fully simulatable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world in a single forward pass. The model accepts multi-view input from a calibrated camera rig and emits a layered output consisting of static and dynamic 3DGS layers, a sky cubemap, and per-camera ISP corrections, while providing native support for non-pinhole camera models via 3DGUT. It reconstructs a 10-20-second multi-camera scene in roughly 1.5 seconds and achieves a PSNR on the Waymo Open Dataset that is 2.01 dB above the strongest evaluated baseline. Instant NuRec is deeply integrated into NuRec and is compatible with AlpaSim for closed-loop simulation.
item.dc:creator: NVIDIA, :, Jiahui Huang, Jiawei Ren, Michal Tyszkiewicz, Bjoern Haefner, Michael Shelley, Xin Kang, Seung Wook Kim, Ning Xu, Qi Wu, Janick Martinez Esturo, Shengyu Huang, Nick Schneider, Laura Leal-Taixe, Zan Gojcic, Sanja Fidler

item.title: Adaptive Volumetric Parameterization of Simply Connected 3-Manifolds with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2608.08672v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Volumetric parameterization, the process of mapping a 3-manifold onto a simplified volumetric domain, is important for many tasks in computer graphics and imaging science. However, most prior volumetric parameterization approaches have only utilized standardized domains such as a solid ball regardless of the overall shape of the given 3-manifolds, which introduces significant geometric distortion and affects the subsequent shape processing and analysis tasks. To overcome this issue, in this work we propose a novel volumetric parameterization framework for simply connected 3-manifolds. Specifically, the proposed framework jointly controls local shape and mass distortions, while adapting the target domain during the optimization process. It enables three progressively more flexible target-domain settings for the parameterization: a prescribed solid ellipsoid, a volume-normalized adaptive ellipsoid with variable radii, and a sea-embedded free-boundary domain. For each setting, the parameterization algorithm consists of a 3D quasi-conformality shape update, a diffusion-based density-equalizing update, and a geometric correction procedure for removing element foldings, thereby allowing for volumetric parameterizations with different desired effects. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Moreover, our framework can be easily applied to multiresolution and localized adaptive volumetric remeshing, volumetric registration, and volumetric morphing. Altogether, our work provides a new way for the representation, processing, and analysis of 3-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Lyu, Qiguang Chen, Lok Ming Lui, Gary P. T. Choi

item.title: Resolution-free neural surrogates for geometric parameterization and mapping with spatially varying fields
item.description: arXiv:2605.28551v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many imaging problems require computing spatial transformations induced by spatially varying intensity, feature, or density fields. Canonical examples include distortion correction, deformable image registration, atlas-based segmentation, and deformation-driven image analysis. These tasks can be formulated as geometric mapping problems in which the transformation is constrained to preserve local structure, control boundary behavior, or regulate angular distortion. Such formulations typically lead to variational models, diffusion processes, or elliptic partial differential equations. However, repeatedly solving high-resolution systems becomes computationally expensive when the underlying parameter fields vary across instances. In this work, we propose a resolution-free neural surrogate for geometric parameterization and mapping problems. Given a spatially varying parameter field $p:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^m$ and grid nodes $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N\subset\Omega$, the model predicts mapped locations $\{u(x_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ on structured grids of different sizes without retraining. To avoid dependence on a fixed grid, we use a multi-resolution geometric encoding strategy that conditions the network on coordinate-augmented samples of the parameter field. The model is trained without labeled solution data by enforcing geometry-aware constraints derived from variational energies, diffusion-based density equalization, and quasi-conformal theory. Experimental results on quasi-conformal mapping and density-equalizing mapping problems are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Yanwen Huang, Lok Ming Lui, Gary P. T. Choi

item.title: Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting with a Multi-GPU PyTorch Backend
item.description: arXiv:2606.11390v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gaussian splatting methods have become increasingly popular for neural reconstruction of the real world. However, they are often limited in scale and resolution due to compute and memory constraints. We present a multi-GPU Gaussian splatting approach that scales reconstruction to higher resolutions and larger scenes while abstracting away the code complexity typically associated with distributing a model. We demonstrate city-scale reconstructions with street-level detail consisting of over 1 billion Gaussian splats. To accomplish this, we propose a PyTorch backend that distributes parameters and operators across GPUs via CUDA unified memory, with optional NVLink support. Because distribution occurs at the operator level, the model code requires no explicit cross-device communication. More broadly, the backend exposes multiple GPUs as an aggregate asynchronous PyTorch device and supports a broad set of PyTorch operators enabling the distribution of general PyTorch workloads.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cong, Francis Williams, Jonathan Swartz, Mark Harris, Sanja Fidler, Ken Museth
